messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: geom_polygon()
parts: I'm not sure I completely get what you want to do, but this works with your code. I'm not sure the area under the curve that you want is really represented well, but perhaps it will get you started?

library(ggplot2)
x<-seq(-3,3,length.out=100)
y<-dnorm(x)

region.x<-x[1<=x&x<=2]
region.y<-y[1<=x&x<=2]

df<-data.frame(x,y)
dfsub<-data.frame(region.x, region.y)

ggplot()+
geom_line(data=df, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
geom_abline(data=df, aes(intercept=0,slope=0),color="red") +
geom_polygon(data=dfsub, aes(region.x,region.y),fill="yellow",color="blue",alpha=0.5) +
labs(title="lsjdfk",x="sdfsd",y="ddsfsa")

messages.subject: Re: geom_polygon()
parts:
Hi:

Is this what you want?

# Data frame to delimit the region to be shaded
DF <- data.frame(x = seq(1, 2, by = 0.01))
DF$y <- dnorm(DF$x)

# Data frame to establish the x-limits of dnorm() for use
# in stat_function()
Dfun <- data.frame(x = c(-3, 3))

# Use geom_ribbon() to produce the shaded region and
# stat_function() to produce the density curve
ggplot(Dfun, aes(x = x)) +
geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
geom_ribbon(data = DF, aes(x = x, ymin = 0, ymax = y), fill = "yellow",
color = "blue") +
stat_function(fun = "dnorm")

Dennis
